# Xisto patches to BearSSL

Base: BearSSL master `7bea48e` (see `VERSION.xisto`), MIT. Every change is marked
`Xisto patch` in the source. Generated files are regenerated with
`tools/regen-bearssl.sh` and checked in; a normal build needs only a C compiler.

Measured on an Apple M4, server CPU per full TLS 1.2 handshake (ECDHE P-256,
ECDSA P-256 certificate), in memory (`bench/tls/crypto.sh`):

| step | µs |
|---|---:|
| BearSSL master, unpatched | 335 |
| 1. native cipher-suite lookup and chunked skip in the handshake code | 250 |
| 2. fixed-base comb for P-256 generator multiplication | 192 |
| 3. 64-bit Montgomery tail for P-256 ECDSA signatures | 165 |
| 4. AArch64 assembly for the P-256 field multiplication | 150 |

1. **`src/ssl/ssl_hs_common.t0`** (regenerates `ssl_hs_client.c`, `ssl_hs_server.c`):
   `cipher-suite-to-elements` walked the cipher-suite table byte by byte in the
   T0 interpreter on every lookup (about half of the 88k interpreted
   instructions of a server handshake; 26k after). It is now a native word with
   a `switch` generated from the same table. `skip-blob` skipped ignored bytes
   one interpreted call per byte (a modern ClientHello carries a 1.2 KB
   post-quantum key share BearSSL ignores); it now skips in chunks, still
   feeding the handshake hash. Regenerating the unpatched sources with our
   build of T0Comp reproduces BearSSL's files byte for byte.
2. **`src/ec/ec_p256_m64.c` + `ec_p256_m64_comb.h`**: `k*G` used a 4-bit
   window (256 doublings, 64 additions). The table holds `j * 16^i * G` for the
   64 nibble positions (61 KB of read-only data, generated by
   `tools/gen_p256_comb.c` from BearSSL's own code): 64 mixed additions, no
   doubling, rows read in full and selected by masks (constant time). The
   incomplete addition is safe for `0 < k < n`, the existing contract.
   Test: `tests/crypto/p256_comb.c` against the generic multiplication and the
   independent m31 implementation.
3. **`src/ec/ecdsa_i31_sign_raw.c`**: for P-256, `s = k^-1 (m + x r) mod n`
   is computed with 4x64-bit Montgomery arithmetic (inversion by `k^(n-2)`,
   4-bit fixed window over the public exponent) instead of 31-bit limbs.
   Test: `tests/crypto/p256_sign.c`, signatures byte-identical to BearSSL's
   original function (they are deterministic) and verified by the m31 code.
4. **`src/ec/ec_p256_m64_arm64.S`**: `f256_montymul` for AArch64, interleaved
   CIOS with the shift-only reduction that `p = -1 mod 2^64` allows; no
   branches, no secret-dependent addresses. Other architectures keep the C
   code. Test: `tests/crypto/p256_montymul.c`, equal modulo p to the C version
   on edge and millions of random inputs, including aliasing.

Other build-level changes: compiled with `-DBR_USE_GETENTROPY=1` (one syscall
to seed each connection, instead of opening `/dev/urandom`).
